text: One pitfall of being savvy about personal finance is getting requests from friends and readers to advise them on their financial situation. On a blog, it’s easy enough to say whatever we want and cover it with a disclaimer that we’re not professionals and this shouldn’t be construed as professional advice, etc. Yet if we’re approached by a good friend or relative and if it seems we could help them, then it’s hard to say no. For instance, several of my aunts read my blog. One approached me about her retirement plan. She asked me to look at a fund of funds she was considering. It was Canadian, but similar to those US target retirement funds which are a mixture of stock and bond funds.

London to Oxford via the Thames Valley — A longer, flatter route following the Thames upstream through Berkshire and Oxfordshire. Around 70 miles in total, passing through Windsor, Henley-on-Thames, and the beautiful Chiltern countryside. An outstanding summer day’s riding from the capital. The Green Chain Walk Cycling Route — A network of connected green spaces in south-east London linking the Thames at Thamesmead to Crystal Palace. Less well-known than some of the capital’s major routes but genuinely rewarding for riders who want to explore London’s surprisingly rural south-east.

Table of Contents 5 ways pediatric dentistry promotes lifelong healthy smiles comes down to prevention, early guidance, and care that fits the way children actually behave and develop. Pediatric dental care is not just a smaller version of adult dentistry. It is built around baby teeth, changing bites, growing jaws, and the very real fact that children need a different kind of support to feel safe and cooperate. A cavity in a baby tooth can seem easy to dismiss. After all, that tooth will fall out. The trouble is that untreated decay can cause pain, infection, trouble eating, and even problems with speech and sleep. Baby teeth also hold space for adult teeth. When they are lost too early, crowding and alignment issues often follow.

But as the stakes grow higher and the consequences of failure become clearer, Artemis realizes that the ultimate challenge may be convincing himself to let go of his own ego and work towards a greater good. "Field Notes from a Catastrophe" is a gripping tale of survival, resilience, and the indomitable human spirit. The novel follows the life of protagonist, Dr. Emily Harper, a renowned climatologist, who is on a mission to Antarctica to study the effects of global warming. However, her life takes a dramatic turn when a sudden and catastrophic climate event traps her and her team in the icy wilderness. The novel vividly portrays their struggle for survival against the harsh elements, dwindling supplies, and the constant threat of hypothermia. As the team's leader, Emily must make tough decisions, often risking her life to ensure the survival of her team. The narrative is interspersed with Emily's field notes, which provide a chilling account of the rapidly changing climate and its devastating effects.

It is quite clear that Cardiff is here to make some noise in 2012. The team has switched from its traditional blue and white kits to red, and the club’s motto is now “Fire & Passion.” The previously injured Stephen McPhail figures to be in the midfield for the Bluebirds, and they are going to hope to use a bunch of injury returnees to produce a great result to start off the season. Captain Mark Hudson is ready to go, and that’s perhaps the biggest addition to the team once again. David Marshall is going to be back in the pipes, just as he was for 47 of Cardiff’s 48 matches last year in the Championship. Leading scorer Peter Whittingham is still back to man the midfield as well, and that’s no shock for the only man to play in all 48 fixtures last year for Cardiff. Also note that this is the first League Championship fixture for summer signing Craig Bellamy, which is as big of a signing as the Bluebirds have had in years.

When the coronavirus pandemic cancelled live music around the world, US musician Stu Brooks decided to take action. The bass player and producer set up the website SaveOurStages.com to lobby for government support for the beleaguered industry. It is now one of the most high-profile grassroots campaigns in the US - and Brooks tells the BBC's Janet Babin how it all started. I started SaveOurStages.com on 23 March, the day that New York City shut down. Like a lot of people in the music industry, I was in shock. And I thought, "what can I do to help?".

If only a few of your teeth are missing, partial dentures are a good solution for replacing them. Unlike a full set of dentures, these are held in place by a plastic base that is the same color as your gums. A metal framework is typically created in order to secure the base and prevent it from falling out. As long as you have natural teeth in place, you cannot wear a full set, so a partial set of dentures is necessary. We treat patients throughout the Kendall area that want to know if a partial set is better than a cosmetic procedure. They function differently because dentures are removable and cosmetic dentistry solutions are typically permanent.
